page: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is a burstable, budget-friendly virtual machine instance belonging to the e2 family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs allocated from a shared physical core, specifically utilizing an eighth of a physical core with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 1.0 GB of system memory, providing 0.5 GB of RAM per core, and does not include any local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the bottom 10% across all evaluated categories. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 132.9 and 171.0, respectively. Memory bandwidth is highly constrained, with cached small-block read speeds reaching 9.73 GB/sec, while uncached large-block read and write speeds drop to 0.1 GB/sec and 1.33 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores also fall into the lowest tier, reflecting the shared-core resource limits, while static web serving throughput is measured at 0.17 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-micro is designed as a low-cost entry point for workloads with minimal resource demands. The shared-core CPU allocation and low memory density make it unsuitable for database operations, data science, or high-throughput web serving. Instead, this instance is best suited for lightweight background tasks, basic development environments, simple cron jobs, or low-traffic utility services that can tolerate variable CPU performance and low memory availability.
